The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages failed for some shoppers
Why, in plain words: A software update changed the format the shop uses to save each shopper's spending summary, and the copies of the shop still running the previous version expected the old format, could not read the new entries, and failed the account page.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 9m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 26.0% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 3,262.30 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages failed for some shoppers while io-shop ran 696c33a
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 01:57 to 02:06 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 8 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 02:13:43 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 02:04:49 UTC
Ended by: Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 01:57 UTC and was back to normal at 02:06 UTC, 9 minutes later. 18.7% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 26.0% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 3,262.30 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. A software update changed the format the shop uses to save each shopper's spending summary, and the copies of the shop still running the previous version expected the old format, could not read the new entries, and failed the account page. What Argus did: rolled back the deployment of io-shop (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Code-Fix kept none of the fix it wrote, which helps only once code outside the repository changes as well: writing it again is AI-2. Argus left automatic sync of io-shop off, to be turned back on once its repository says what should run (AI-3). Deploying the same revision again, or any revision that writes the two-field cache entries, could make account pages fail again while replicas of the earlier revision are still serving.

Impact
9m 0s - onset until back to normal
26.0% - peak error rate
2,022 - requests failed
1.0% to 18.7% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
3,262.30 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The new code changed what a summary cache entry holds, from a bare figure in cents to an 'amount/items' text, and wrote it where the previous version also reads, with no versioned key or other way to keep the two shapes apart. Replicas still on the previous version share that cache during the paused rolling update, and their reader expects a bare cents figure, so it raised ValueError on the new entries and the account page request failed.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the share of the service's requests that failed rose well above its usual level.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
    G3714 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ValueError: summary cache entry '2400/8' is not a figure in cents at src/io_shop/summary_cache.py - 13 occurrences in 7 minutes, 01:58–02:04
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 33 occurrences in 38 minutes, 01:27–02:04; # was 0.50% to 26.00%, typically 1.50%, highest at 01:59
why 1 Those requests failed because reading the shopper's summary cache entry in src/io_shop/summary_cache.py raised a ValueError: the entry was an 'amount/items' text, not a figure in cents.
  Evidence:
    G3714
    Gc956 ERROR io-shop: summary cache entry could not be read - ValueError: summary cache entry '2400/8' is not a figure in cents at src/io_shop/summary_cache.py (# of 200 requests) - 7 occurrences in 7 minutes, 01:58–02:04; # was 30 to 51, typically 41, highest at 01:59
why 2 Entries in that two-field shape came from revision 696c33a, deployed at 01:58:24 UTC. It changed a cache entry from a bare figure in cents to one text holding the figure and the number of purchases behind it.
  Evidence:
    P2 01:58:24 UTC deploy 696c33a by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision 696c33a to io-shop, compared against 5470c1a - the revision deployed before it.
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy of revision 5470c1a (P1). The metrics read back over the hours after it show the service at its usual error rate until the onset, account pages logged as rendering normally after it, and the confirmed rollback left that revision running with the service back to normal.
      T4 02:05:09 Investigator Agent: Read back 361 minutes of metrics
      Gad41 INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 5 occurrences in 17 minutes, 01:30–01:46
      M1 02:05:29 Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1: confirmed, still in place
      T21 02:07:07 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 02:06
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:05:23.
      T17
why 3 The new shape broke pages because, as read at 02:05:13 UTC, the rolling update was paused with 3 replicas still on revision 5470c1a, and those replicas could not read the two-field entries.
  Evidence:
    T9 02:05:13 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - 3 of 6 replicas run revision 696c33a, deployed at 01:58:24, and 3 still run revision 5470c1a, of a deployment sized for 3; its rolling update is paused
    D1
    Gc956
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that tested the change against the previous revision reading the same cache, such as a mixed-version compatibility test, before a change to the shape of a shared cache entry went out. (AI-4, AI-5)
- The previous revision's cache reader fails the account page when it meets an entry it cannot read, instead of treating the entry as a miss and working the figure out, which is what the module's own docstring says should happen. (AI-6)
- No rollout health gate was seen that halts and rolls back an io-shop rolling update when errors rise. The rollout stayed in place, with both revisions serving, until Argus rolled it back. (AI-7)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | Revision 696c33a was deployed at 01:58:24 UTC and the rolling update paused with 3 of 6 replicas on it and 3 still on 5470c1a. The new revision writes summary cache entries as 'amount/items' (e.g. '2400/8'), and the old revision's reader expects a bare cents figure. Account-page requests that cross between the two versions fail with ValueError, so the error rate stepped to about 20-26%. | 0.85 | confirmed
C2 | Revision 696c33a shipped a change to the summary cache entry format that fails account pages. This is the alternative reading in which the code is at fault, if the rollout were judged converged. | 0.10 | confirmed, as tested for C1

Trigger
io-shop was deployed from 5470c1a to 696c33a at 01:58:24 UTC, by kuki.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 02:05:29 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 01:57 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 02:04:26 UTC, 7 minutes 26 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Write the fix again: its change to the repository and the change outside the repository that Code-Fix's reading names, made together - Code-Fix kept none of the fix it wrote | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a CI test that runs the previous revision's summary cache reader against entries written by the new revision, and the reverse, so a change to a shared entry shape cannot ship if a mixed rollout would break it. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Make it a review rule that any change to the shape of a shared cache entry either writes under a new versioned key or first ships a reader that accepts both shapes, before the writer changes. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Add a test that every summary cache reader treats an entry it cannot parse as a miss and falls back to working out the figure, never failing the page. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Add an error-rate health gate to io-shop rolling updates that halts the rollout and rolls it back automatically when the error rate rises above its baseline. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-8 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came 6 minutes 26 seconds after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
- 47 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - 3 of 6 replicas run revision 696c33a, deployed at 01:58:24, and 3 still run revision 5470c1a, of a deployment sized for 3; its rolling update is paused.
- 57 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 02:05:23.
- 1 minute 3 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1.
- 2 minutes 41 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- The Code-Fix Agent kept none of the fix it wrote, once its reading showed the fix would help only together with a change outside the repository.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What Code-Fix read in the source - nothing ran to check it
F1 | Yes. The patch moves this revision's reader to a versioned key (summary_key), but nothing in this repository writes entries into the cache. SummaryEntry.__str__ produces the text, and the lookup seam LookUpSummary is supplied from outside, so the code that stores entries lives elsewhere. Today that outside writer puts '2400/8' under the bare shopper id, which is the key replicas still on 5470c1a read. Until it writes under summary_key(shopper_id) instead, those replicas keep meeting two-field entries and keep failing. The patch alone wouldn't spare users anything: worse, this revision would stop reading its own entries, which only makes it slower. To fix this, the cache-population code outside this repo has to write under summary_key(shopper_id) (summary-v2:{shopper_id}). Or it has to stop writing the two-field shape under the old key until no replica runs 5470c1a. Separately, the old revision's reader is already deployed and can only be changed by shipping a new build, not from this repo's current code.
How the code outside Code-Fix's patch uses what it changes, read on main
U1 | cached_summary at src/io_shop/account_page.py:237, in _the_figure_for: calls it: found = cached_summary(account.shopper_id, look_up_summary, cache_endpoint)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, some io-shop shoppers could not load their account pages. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. A software update changed the format the shop uses to save each shopper's spending summary. Copies of the shop still running the previous version expected the old format, could not read the new entries, and failed the account page. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so no on-call responder was called in. Argus ended the incident by rolling back the io-shop deployment. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.
